title: Four consumed surfaces of the appeal have no dependency row, and the plan carries no contract, integration or external dependency for either slice
source: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP table rows DP-03, DP-07, DP-08, DP-13 and DP-19 and section R5.4 dependency classes; the metadata rows of RWB-S4-E5014-APP (Depends on (build) = RWB-S4-E5014-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON; Contract dependencies = None; Integration dependencies = None; External dependencies = None) and of RWB-S4-E5014-CON (all None); the ownership rows owned by S4 in _work/msr/context/S4.md; TSD S4 v2 T-A.1 and T6.1; FSD S4 v3 A2.14.2 (Integration points LIT, Workbench) and A2.14.1 (prerequisite FEAT-LIT-12); legacy RWB-E5-014 Depends on FEAT-LIT-12
section: Sections 3, 12.2, 12.8 and 13 of both stories, and the metadata tables; the ops_consumed key of both fragments
description: The two slices consume four surfaces that no metadata row carries. (1) The D7.4 approval of rwb-decision, which R-LIT-46 and R-LIT-47 make the decision point of the appeal and which the approval contract of P7 publishes, with the above-limit approval of the Head of Litigation. (2) The rwb-case contract that reads the case route state and answers the route facts APPEAL_DECISION, APPEAL_FILED, IN_HEARING and TO_WRITE_OFF, because the case of record and all five route states of the appeal are P3's. (3) The rwb-partner firm instruction that R-LIT-47 requires ('instruct the firm to appeal and reset the hearing timers'). (4) The reference-data read of LOV-LEGAL-TYPE and LOV-LEGAL-STATUS, because DP-07 is not in either slice's pattern set while TSD S4 T3.2 makes both lists required for action_type and status; the declared Litigation right of each operation is in the same position, because DP-08 is not in the set either. The approval contract is a P7 contract story of an earlier wave and would be a C dependency that never blocks; the case and partner contracts have no CON story in the plan and are built against their fakes; and the operation names of the case read and the firm instruction are given by no source at all, so they are carried as the placeholder. A reader of the metadata alone would conclude that the appeal needs only its own contract and the two platform contracts.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5: DP-03 adds H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, DP-07 adds H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON, DP-08 adds H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and C RWB-P4-E1037-CON, DP-19 adds H RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the patterns applied to both slices are DP03, DP13 and DP19, and both slices list Contract, Integration and External dependencies as None; _work/msr/context/S4.md gives S4 five REST operations provided and no consumed operation, two tables (hearing, legal_action), no event, no job and one workflow (LitigationWorkflow); TSD S4 v2 T-A.1 holds API-S4-001 to API-S4-005 of rwb-litigation and no operation of rwb-case, rwb-decision or rwb-partner; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-LIT-46, R-LIT-47 and R-LIT-49 name 'Approver at D7.4', 'Panel law firm' and 'Write-off team with Credit Administration' as owners of steps this service does not own
area: Dependency map and build sequencing, S4 rwb-litigation with P7 rwb-decision, P3 rwb-case, S9 rwb-partner and P4 rwb-access
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P7 rwb-decision, P3 rwb-case, S9 rwb-partner architects and the platform team
proposed: Carry the four as non-blocking consumed rows in the Dependency Map: the approval contract as a C dependency of its wave, the case and partner contracts as published contracts built against their fakes, and the reference-data contract RWB-P3-E1043-CON as a C dependency, with the declared right of each operation as the edge and guard rule of DP-08; name the case read, the route facts and the instruction request in the case and partner contract stories when they are written, and leave the metadata rows of both slices as the plan gives them.

title: The appeal grounds that legacy AC1 records are neither a column of legal_action nor a field of the FSD catalog
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E5-014 (AC1: 'records the appeal decision, the grounds and the approval'); TSD S4 v2 T3.1 (legal_action, DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014) and T3.2; FSD S4 v3 A2.14.3.2 field catalog (eight fields, none of them the grounds) and A2.14.4.1 (AC-S4-014-01); Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-LIT-14
section: Sections 1, 2, 4, 8, 11 and 13 of RWB-S4-E5014-APP; sections 2, 11, 12 and 13 of RWB-S4-E5014-CON; the Data tables of both stories
description: Legacy AC1 requires the story to record 'the appeal decision, the grounds and the approval'. The decision has a home (the decision record through DP-03, with its final call and its decision code) and the approval has a home (rwb-decision), but the grounds have none: legal_action carries fourteen fields in TSD S4 T3.1 and none of them is a grounds field, a grounds text or a grounds document reference, and the FSD field catalog of A2.14.3.2 names eight fields of the same row, none of which is the grounds either. No attachment reference to rwb-document is given for this feature. Adding a column would invent a data element that no data model, no schema and no dictionary row approves, and inventing an element in the contract would fix the invented name for every later legal action. The grounds are therefore absent from the row, from the contract's elements and from every table of both stories, and the placeholder is used wherever the story must name them.
evidence: TSD S4 v2 T3.1 legal_action: DF-LEG-001 id, DF-LEG-002 case_id, DF-LEG-003 law_firm_id, DF-LEG-004 action_type, DF-LEG-005 lawsuit_no, DF-LEG-006 black_case_no, DF-LEG-007 red_case_no, DF-LEG-008 court_name, DF-LEG-009 claim_amount, DF-LEG-010 filed_date, DF-LEG-011 judgment_date, DF-LEG-012 judgment_amount, DF-LEG-013 lit_status, DF-LEG-014 status; FSD S4 v3 A2.14.3.2 lists case_id, law_firm_id, action_type, lawsuit_no, black_case_no, red_case_no, court_name and claim_amount only; the FSD data tables repeat the same eight fields for A2.14; no source read for this key names a grounds column, a grounds table or an attachment reference for the appeal
area: Data model and contract, S4 rwb-litigation with P5 rwb-document
owner_role: Data steward and business analyst, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P5 rwb-document owner
proposed: Decide where the grounds live and write it once in the logical data model: either a new legal_action column with a dictionary row (a new major version of the DDL template and of the contract), or the grounds as a document of rwb-document referenced from the decision record's inputs reference as the app story builds it. Until then both stories carry the placeholder and no column.

title: The legacy master carries no requirement identifier for RWB-E5-014, so both slices trace to the feature only
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E5-014 (metadata table: Epic, Module, Feature FEAT-LIT-14, Process, Priority Must, Depends on FEAT-LIT-12, Decision None); _work/msr/plan/legacy_index.json entry RWB-E5-014 with reqs = []; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md row FEAT-LIT-14; FSD S4 v3 Requirements served (REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010)
section: Sections 2 and 18 of both stories; the reqs key of both fragments
description: The legacy story RWB-E5-014 carries no REQ identifier: its metadata table names the feature FEAT-LIT-14 and the prerequisite FEAT-LIT-12 and no requirement row, the plan's legacy index records an empty requirement list, and the FSD S4 requirements table lists ten requirements of the module whose texts cover notices, the pack, the panel, court tracking, settlement, appeal approval, enforcement, deferral and proceeds but names no requirement identifier for the appeal feature itself. The Epics 3 to 8 specification gives the feature one row and no requirement. Both slices therefore trace to FEAT-LIT-14 and to the L3 process 08 Litigate and enforce, and the requirement column carries the placeholder until the Epics 3 to 8 PRD of the module adds the identifiers. Nothing blocks the build; the exposure is a traceability report that cannot roll the story up to a requirement.
evidence: The metadata table of RWB-E5-014 has seven rows and no requirement row; the legacy index of the run records reqs: [] for the key; FSD S4 v3 'Requirements served' lists REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010 and its A2.14 section gives no requirement identifier; the Epics 3 to 8 specification row for FEAT-LIT-14 gives Epic E5, Module S4, Kind User, Primary role Litigation officer, Systems LIT and Workbench, Depends on FEAT-LIT-12 and no requirement
area: Traceability and requirements, EP05, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: Business analyst, S4 rwb-litigation, with the PRD owner of EP05
proposed: Add one requirement row to the Epics 3 to 8 PRD and to the S4 module trace, covering the appeal decision with its grounds and approval and the tracking to the hearing, and rewrite the requirement column of both stories and of their fragments when it exists.

title: No value of LOV-LEGAL-STATUS names an appeal decision or a declined appeal, and the appeal's own states are case route states
source: TSD S4 v2 T3.2 (LOV-LEGAL-STATUS: OPEN, FILED, JUDGMENT, ENFORCING, CLOSED, WITHDRAWN) and T3.1 (DF-LEG-014); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 state table rows JUDGMENT_DISMISSED, APPEAL_DECISION, APPEAL_FILED, IN_HEARING and TO_WRITE_OFF and rules R-LIT-45 to R-LIT-49; legacy RWB-E5-014 AC1; FSD S4 v3 A2.14
section: Section 8 (BR8), section 9 and section 10 of RWB-S4-E5014-APP; sections 9, 11 and 12 of RWB-S4-E5014-CON; the acs and assumptions of both fragments
description: The appeal is a legal action, and a legal action's status has six values in TSD S4 T3.2. None of the six names an appeal decision, a declined appeal or an appeal in progress: the states the rules actually move the case through are JUDGMENT_DISMISSED, APPEAL_DECISION, APPEAL_FILED, IN_HEARING and TO_WRITE_OFF, which the state table of the Business Rules and Routing Logic gives as states of the litigation machine that rwb-case holds. Reading them as legal-action statuses would fork the vocabulary and make one word mean two things across two services; keeping the row on the six values leaves no value that names the decision or the refusal. The two slices therefore declare the case route states as rwb-case's, and let the decision and the refusal live on the decision record, while the row uses OPEN, FILED and WITHDRAWN only. Which value a declined appeal carries is a design ruling and not a source value, and it is recorded here so that a reviewer can see it.
evidence: TSD S4 v2 T3.2 'LOV-LEGAL-STATUS | OPEN, FILED, JUDGMENT, ENFORCING, CLOSED, WITHDRAWN'; TSD S4 T4 'LITIGATION. 79 rules over 38 states'; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 state table: JUDGMENT_DISMISSED (Exception, dismissed or lost), APPEAL_DECISION (Decision point, D7.4), APPEAL_FILED (Partner step, firm files); rules R-LIT-46 to R-LIT-49 write those states as case states, not as legal_action.status values
area: State model, S4 rwb-litigation with P3 rwb-case
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P3 rwb-case architect and the business analyst of S4
proposed: Keep the case route states with rwb-case and the six list values with the legal action, and record the mapping once in the logical data model: OPEN from the window opening, FILED when the firm files, WITHDRAWN when the approver declines or the appeal is not pursued, with the decision and its reason on the decision record. If the business needs a status of its own for a decided or a declined appeal, add it to LOV-LEGAL-STATUS as a versioned change and raise a new major version of the contract.

title: The length of the appeal window and the filing deadline of R-LIT-47 are given by no source read, though both rules turn on them
source: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-LIT-45 (service level 'to the appeal window end'), R-LIT-46 (condition 'appeal_window_ends is in the future', service level 'to the window end') and R-LIT-47 (service level 'to the filing deadline'); TSD S4 v2 T4 and T3.1 (no window or deadline column); FSD S4 v3 A2.14.3.1 (VR-S4-014-1 and BR-S4-014 only); legacy RWB-E5-014 AC1 and its message MSG-S4-002
section: Sections 2, 3, 4, 8, 12.6 and 13 of RWB-S4-E5014-APP; sections 11, 12.6 and 13 of RWB-S4-E5014-CON; the assumptions of both fragments
description: R-LIT-46 fires only while appeal_window_ends is in the future and R-LIT-47 has to file before a deadline; both are durable timers of this service's workflow, and neither length is stated anywhere: the rule table gives the service levels as 'to the window end' and 'to the filing deadline' and no figure, the legal_action row has no window or deadline column, the FSD validation and business rules of A2.14.3.1 give only the required-field check and the no-value-in-code rule, and the legacy story gives no interval. The two lengths are therefore versioned reference rows read with their version, and their content is carried as the placeholder in both stories. A guessed figure would put a legal deadline into code and would be wrong for at least one court and one product group.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4: R-LIT-45 service level 'To the appeal window end', R-LIT-46 condition 'appeal_window_ends is in the future' with service level 'To the window end', R-LIT-47 service level 'To the filing deadline'; TSD S4 v2 T3.1 has no appeal window, deadline or review-date field; FSD S4 v3 A2.14.3.1 gives VR-S4-014-1 (required field) and BR-S4-014 (no value in code) and no interval; the legacy story names MSG-S4-002 'The claim on this case expires on {date}. File before then.' with no window length
area: Reference data and timers, S4 rwb-litigation with the business owner of the litigation route
owner_role: Business analyst and business owner, S4 rwb-litigation
proposed: Publish the appeal window length and the filing deadline as versioned reference rows of the litigation route, with their effective dates and the product groups they apply to, and reference those rows from R-LIT-46 and R-LIT-47; until then both stories read them as reference data at their version in force and carry the placeholder.
